transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-07
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes (calculated)
Attendees: Ari Chen (Redwood AE); Samira Patel (Redwood SE); Liam O'Connor (TensorWorks Head of Partnerships); Priya Desai (TensorWorks - Cloud Partnerships); Marco Ruiz (TensorWorks Solutions Architect)
Recording id: fireflies-20250507-tensorworks-001

Auto-summary (auto): Intro call to explore partnership between Redwood Inference and TensorWorks. Focus areas: private deployment options on TensorWorks GPUs, technical integration (drivers, runtimes), pricing and joint GTM. Action items captured.

Topics: partner intro; deployment modes (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private); security/compliance; benchmarking and POC; commercial/B2B GTM.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ari Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Ari from Redwood, I'm the AE on the partnership side, super excited to meet the TensorWorks team.
[00:08] Liam O'Connor: Hey Ari, hi Samira, thanks for setting this up, yeah Liam here, we run partnerships at TensorWorks.
[00:12] Priya Desai: Hi all, Priya, works on cloud partnerships, happy to be here.
[00:16] Samira Patel: Hi! Samira here, I'm the solutions engineer, I'll walk a little bit through the technical bits if that's cool.
[00:20] Marco Ruiz: Marco Ruiz, solutions architect on the TensorWorks side.

[00:22] Ari Chen: Quick agenda - intros, high level overviews, then Samira will run technical details and we can go into POC/benchmarks and commercial. Any additions?
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: Nope sounds good. Maybe also touch on go-to-market and what partner motions look like.

[00:35] Ari Chen: Perfect. I'll give a 2-minute Redwood overview - we are an inference platform, we run hosted API, dedicated reserved GPU pools, and private deployments for customers that want their own VPCs or on-prem. We optimize for latency, cost, and reliability and provide tooling like observability and rollouts.
[00:52] Liam O'Connor: Great, quick question - when you say private deployment, is that full control on the partner infra or do customers still reach Redwood control plane?
[01:02] Samira Patel: Uh yeah good question. There are modes - we have a private control plane option where the customer owns the network and we run a customer-managed control plane, and then for some partners we do a partner-hosted option. We can clarify depending on business terms.
[01:16] Priya Desai: When you run on partner hosts, what's the billing model typically, do you do per-token or is it a capacity reserve model?
[01:24] Ari Chen: There's flexibility - hosted is per-usage per-token, Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits, and Private setups tend to be license + infra ops or a platform fee plus support. For partner integrations we can do revenue share or reseller models depending on the partner.

[01:40] Marco Ruiz: From a technical view we care about driver compatibility, runtimes (CUDA, ROCm), and also the KV cache and the way you manage batching. Are you shipping native runtimes or are there pieces that need to be installed on our side?
[01:54] Samira Patel: We have a GPU-optimized serving runtime that we ship - it's containerized, expects Nvidia CUDA or AMD ROCm depending on the hardware. There's a light agent/daemon for metrics and KV cache hooks. In partner-hosted scenarios we provide deployment manifests and a small control-plane component. Sometimes the naming in docs is a bit messy - like we say KV cache and it's K-V, uh we know naming is inconsistent across ecosystems.
[02:18] Liam O'Connor: Yeah that naming thing is familiar. Is your runtime open source or closed?
[02:23] Ari Chen: It's proprietary currently, but we provide partner libraries and images; we do signed images and can support air-gapped installs for on-prem partners.

[02:31] Priya Desai: Security is a big piece for our enterprise customers - do you support KMS integrations and hardware HSM?
[02:37] Samira Patel: Yes. KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and commonly used HSMs) are supported. We also have audit logs and RBAC; for stricter workflows we do SOC 2 documentation and can undergo security review.
[02:49] Marco Ruiz: How do you handle secrets - do you keep any key materials in Redwood control plane in private mode?
[02:55] Samira Patel: In private deployments we can make sure keys are customer-managed and never leave their VPC. For partner-hosted deployments it's configurable, but we default to customer KMS.

[03:05] Liam O'Connor: Good. On the performance side - what's your typical latency numbers and do you have profiles for different instance types?
[03:12] Ari Chen: We publish performance profiles per model and hardware pairing - for example a 70B on A10g-like class gets X token/s in our benchmarks, but obviously it depends on quantization, KV cache reuse, and sequence length. We'll share our profile sheet.
[03:26] Marco Ruiz: We run mixed workloads - short chat-like generation and some long-form completions. How does batching affect latency if you run on TensorWorks multi-tenant nodes?
[03:36] Samira Patel: We do continuous batching and workload-aware batching; it's tuned so tail-latency stays in SLOs. On multi-tenant nodes you can pin reserved capacity or use burst pools to avoid noisy neighbors. That is a common tradeoff - latency vs utilization.

[03:50] Priya Desai: On joint GTM - what partner motions have worked previously for you? Co-sell, referral, marketplace?
[03:57] Ari Chen: PLG is our big motion but for partners it's often referral + co-sell for larger deals. Marketplaces are useful too. For GPU partners we sometimes do joint benchmarks and a partner page highlighting validated stacks.

[04:08] Liam O'Connor: Perfect. On the integration surface area - is there a documented partner onboarding flow we can review?
[04:14] Ari Chen: Yes, we'll share a partner pack with step-by-step integration docs, the security questionnaire, and sample deployment manifests. That will include sample terraform and helm charts.

[04:22] Marco Ruiz: For the POC we'd like to run a small benchmark - can you provide the bench script and the expected artifacts?
[04:29] Samira Patel: Absolutely. We have a benchmark harness that runs token-throughput and tail-latency tests, plus cost-per-token estimates. We'll provide the script; the usual ask is access to a test VM with same driver stack and a sample model.

[04:42] Ari Chen: Let's talk about one concrete pilot flow: we run a 2-week bench on your infra, we run 3 models (a 7B, 13B, 70B quantized), collect latency and cost metrics, and then compare to Redwood hosted baseline. Does that sound reasonable?
[04:58] Marco Ruiz: Yes, that works. We can provide environment by next week.

[05:02] Priya Desai: On commercial - are there minimums for dedicated pools?
[05:06] Ari Chen: For Dedicated we typically see monthly commits depending on GPU type, but for partner pilots we can do shorter trials and then discuss commit levels if the POC goes well.

[05:15] Liam O'Connor: Who on Redwood will be the point of contact for technical integration?
[05:19] Ari Chen: Samira will own the SE side and I'll own partnership/commercial.

[05:23] Samira Patel: Yep I'll coordinate with Marco on the test environment and runbooks.

[05:28] Marco Ruiz: A couple of additional technical asks - container image signing, license metadata in images, and also GPU isolation when multiple tenants share a node.
[05:37] Samira Patel: We have image signing with signatures and can embed license metadata. For GPU isolation we recommend MPS for NVIDIA in some cases and cgroups/namespace isolation; we can work with your infra team on best practices.

[05:49] Ari Chen: Also, just calling out - some of the customers we work with want region-resident data for compliance, so we need to confirm your region footprint if we do a private deployment for EU customers.
[05:59] Priya Desai: Yes, we have EU regions and we're spinning up APAC later this year.

[06:04] Liam O'Connor: For sales enablement, is there a partner portal or at least partner collateral you can give us to start training our GTM folks?
[06:12] Ari Chen: We'll include a partner one-pager, tech FAQ, and a basic sales playbook in the pack.

[06:18] Priya Desai: On legal side - do you have a standard reseller or referral agreement?
[06:23] Ari Chen: We have templates; I'll loop in our legal if we need to exchange drafts. For pilots we normally use a simple SOW.

[06:30] Marco Ruiz: One more technical note - how do you handle model sharding or offloading? Some of our nodes have limited vRAM per GPU.
[06:38] Samira Patel: We support model parallelism patterns and quantized execution paths; we can also fallback to less-memory variants or split across multiple GPUs - it's part of the runtime's kernel selection and memory planning. We'll surface recommended quantization profiles for common models.

[06:53] Liam O'Connor: Competitors question - some partners mention Paperspace and Lambda Labs, how would you position Redwood vs those for a GPU partner?
[07:01] Ari Chen: Short answer: Redwood is inference-first with a unified API across hosted/dedicated/private and strong observability and rollouts. Competitors offer infra or endpoints, but our emphasis is on predictable inference economics, rollouts, and developer ergonomics.

[07:15] Priya Desai: Sounds good. Any red flags we should be aware of?
[07:19] Samira Patel: Nothing immediate - just typical caveats around driver versions and ensuring the correct ROCm/CUDA stacks for models. We'll surface exact reqs.

[07:26] Ari Chen: Okay let's capture next steps: I will share partner pack and security questionnaire, Samira will share the benchmark harness and runbook, Marco will provision the test VM and model artifact, and TensorWorks will share product brief and preferred SLAs.

[07:41] Liam O'Connor: Yep agreed. Timeline - can we aim to have the POC kickoff by 2025-05-19?

[07:47] Samira Patel: That should be doable, assuming we get access and the infra is ready.

[07:52] Marco Ruiz: We'll try to provide access by 2025-05-11.

[07:56] Ari Chen: Great. Any other questions?

[07:59] Priya Desai: None from me.

[08:01] Ari Chen: Awesome - thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the deck and links.

[08:05] Liam O'Connor: Thanks Ari. Bye.

[08:07] Samira Patel: Thanks all, bye.
